name: Vivigani Airfield
reason: Rule 3: the tourism page names battle airfields only generically; no access, facilities or visit are sourced for this one.
objection: A guide-named WWII site and 716 views; but nothing a visitor can do for half an hour is sourced.

name: No. 2 Strip Milne Bay
reason: Rules 1-3: generic mention of battle airfields only, no pin (Wikipedia point is at sea), nothing to see sourced.
objection: Part of the Battle of Milne Bay heritage the tourism board promotes; but not individually named.

name: Logea Island
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism page names Nuli Sapi on Logea Island (one counted source); rule 2 uncertain since the draw is a resort stay, though a reef island near Samarai.
objection: For: tourism board map highlights it, easy boat ride from Alotau. Against: the named thing is a lodge (operators are not spots) and a single source.

name: Doini Island
reason: Rule 2: privately owned plantation resort island; Wikivoyage lists it only as accommodation.
objection: Wikivoyage Alotau names it with beaches and golf; but access is for resort guests, which is a lodge not a public place.

name: Tawali
reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism board names it first among the world-renowned Milne Bay dive sites; a dive site is a place (the site, not the resort).
objection: Single source, zero views, and the access is via the resort. Counter: a named world-class dive site is the draw of the province.

name: Deacon's Reef
reason: Rule 1: named only in the tourism board's list of dive sites (one counted source); no coordinates, no detail.
objection: For: same source as Tawali calls it world-renowned. Against: one list mention, no pin, no description; cannot be placed without owner-supplied coordinates.

name: Gonubalabala
reason: Rule 1: tourism board names it as a dive site and shows a giant manta ray photo from its waters; a wildlife/dive place.
objection: One source, no pin yet, and the pin must be resolved from a map feature. Counter: named twice on the same page (list and manta caption).

name: Wahoo Point
reason: Rule 1: only a dive-site list mention on the tourism page; no pin or detail.
objection: For: board calls it world-renowned. Against: one bare mention, nothing sourced about what is there, no coordinates.

name: Nuakata Island
reason: Rule 1/2: only a place name in Wikivoyage's custom itinerary text; no visitor facilities or description.
objection: Wikivoyage counts, and it is a tour stop from Alotau; but no sourced thing to do.

name: Suau Coast
reason: Rule 3: a coastal district/tour area, not a place with a point; no article or pin.
objection: Named in itinerary options; but there is no distinct site to pin.

name: Kwato Island
reason: Rule 1: re-looked at Wikivoyage Alotau and Milne Bay; neither names it. Wikipedia only (mission history, 50 residents).
objection: Historic mission with church and tombs; but no visitor source says to go.

name: Kiriwina
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Trobriand Islands names it as the main island (airstrip, lodges, dancing). Risk of duplicating a Trobriand Islands group entry; sources describe the group as one visitor area.
objection: For: the island where all visitors land. Against: near-duplicate of the group entry; dancing is tied to a yam festival (event). Keep only one of Kiriwina or the group.

name: Kitava
reason: Rule 1/3: Wikivoyage only lists it as a major island; part of the Trobriands group.
objection: Tourist vessels stop there with a wreck and reefs; but only Wikipedia says so.

name: Kaileuna
reason: Rule 1/3: only listed as a major island in Wikivoyage; no visitor facilities; part of the Trobriand group.
objection: A named island in the destination article; but no thing to do sourced.

name: Vakuta
reason: Rule 1/3: only listed as a major island in Wikivoyage; part of the Trobriand group.
objection: Same as Kaileuna: named but nothing to see or do.

name: Vanatinai Island
reason: Rule 3: Wikivoyage lists it (as Sudest) among Louisiade islands; the Louisiade Archipelago is the one spot for the group and sources give no separate visitor stop.
objection: Endemic birds and a reef harbour; but no visitor facilities or separate guide listing.

name: Rossel Island
reason: Rule 3: one entry in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list; part of the archipelago spot, no separate visitor stop described.
objection: Large lagoon and wrecks; but sources describe no way to visit.

name: Deboyne Islands
reason: Rule 3: Louisiade island-list entry only; part of the Louisiade group.
objection: Has a small ecotourist resort that yachties and divers use; but the resort is an operator and sourcing is one list line.

name: Calvados Chain
reason: Rule 3: Louisiade island-list entry only; part of the group, nothing visitor-specific.
objection: Wikivoyage names it; but a bare list entry.

name: Duchateau Islands
reason: Rule 3: Louisiade island-list entry only; part of the group.
objection: Wikivoyage names it; but a bare list entry.

name: Panapompom Islands
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; no counted source, only Wikipedia; part of Deboyne/Louisiade.
objection: Resort project; but unsourced to visitors.

name: Conflict Group
reason: Rule 1: re-looked at Wikivoyage Milne Bay and Louisiade; not named. Wikipedia only.
objection: 3,391 views and an eco resort; but no visitor source.

name: Mount Vineuo
reason: Rule 3: highest peak of Goodenough Island, which is being kept as a spot; no trail or access sourced (rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage names the 2,566 m peak; but it is only a mention inside the island entry.

name: Deidei Hot Springs
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; Wikivoyage mentions volcanic activity at Fergusson only generically; Wikipedia alone names it. Fergusson Island's note already covers the hot springs.
objection: Active hot springs are a real draw; but no counted source and no access details.

name: Woodlark Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Milne Bay lists the Woodlarks as an other destination (carvings, reefs); an island group a counted source names as somewhere to go.
objection: Remote and one source, no facilities sourced; but listed as its own destination in the province guide.

name: Dobu Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Milne Bay names it as a most significant small island with volcanic activity (inline in Other destinations, not its own listing); one source.
objection: For: counted source plus 3,097 views, volcanic. Against: no listing of its own, no visitor facilities, little to do.

name: Sanaroa Island
reason: Rule 1: the 'best coral cover' claim is not in Wikivoyage, which only names the island; no visitor detail.
objection: Named as significant by Wikivoyage; but nothing to see or do sourced.
